version.changelog:
- Initial release of AI Interview Coach.
- Generates 10 personalized interview questions based on resume (PDF/Word/MD) or specified job position.
- Produces a markdown document including answer spaces and reference answers for self-assessment.
- Supports both technical and behavioral questions tailored to user input.
- Step-by-step workflow for input handling, question generation, and output formatting.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-interview-coach
Version: 1.0.0

The AI Interview Coach skill is a legitimate tool designed to help users prepare for job interviews by analyzing resumes or job descriptions. The instructions in SKILL.md and README.md are clearly aligned with the stated purpose, focusing on text extraction from various file formats (PDF, Word, Markdown) and generating structured interview questions. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it only describes reading user-provided resumes or job-role text and generating a 10-question markdown interview document, and it does not request extra credentials, unusual binaries, or hidden installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the runtime instructions: the SKILL.md describes reading resumes or job-role input and producing 10 tailored interview questions and reference answers. There are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or config paths required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to identifying input (resume file path or job role), extracting text from markdown/PDF/DOCX, generating questions, and formatting output. The skill asks for file paths and to use appropriate extraction tools but does not instruct the agent to read arbitrary system files, environment variables, or to send data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata shows no install spec and this is instruction-only (lowest risk). The README includes an example 'npx skills add ...' command — that is an installation suggestion outside the SKILL.md metadata and, if used, could execute network-based installer logic from whatever tool 'npx skills' uses. Treat installing via third-party installers with normal caution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no primary credential, and requests no config paths. Its expected access (reading user-supplied resume files) is proportionate to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal). The skill does not request persistent presence or system-wide configuration changes in the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will ask for a resume file path or a job title and then read the provided file to generate interview questions. Before using it: (1) only provide file paths to resumes you intend to share (do not give full-system or sensitive file paths); (2) be cautious if you follow the README's suggested 'npx skills add ...' installer — that runs an installer outside the skill metadata and will fetch code from a registry; (3) verify any installer source/URL before running it, and avoid giving the agent access to unrelated local files or secrets. If you want extra assurance, ask the skill author/source for an explicit install manifest or a signed release URL.
